detailed_rationale:
NLC India is a Navratna central-government-owned corporation engaged in lignite mining and thermal power generation, now diversifying into renewable energy under the Ministry of Coal. Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) consolidated revenue was Rs 5,042 crore with net profit of Rs 1,481 crore, and TTM profit growth of roughly 38%; the company received a Letter of Intent from GUVNL for a 900 MW solar project (July 30, 2026), a genuine, verifiable new-growth catalyst as the company extends beyond its legacy lignite/thermal base into renewables. This diversification is real and worth crediting, but the underlying core business remains a slow-growing one: 5-year sales growth of just 12% and a 3-year quant revenue CAGR of only about 2.7% show this is fundamentally a mature, regulated utility/miner, not a growth story, with the recent 900 MW LoI being additive at the margin rather than transformative relative to the company's existing scale.

The earnings-quality item that must be named plainly: FY26 other income was a substantial Rs 1,887 crore, flagged explicitly by available financial commentary as inflating reported earnings -- for a PSU miner/generator, such other income typically includes interest on cash/investment balances and/or regulatory or subsidy-related recoveries, and treating the reported profit growth (and the ROE figure derived from it) as pure core-operations performance would overstate the underlying business's earning power. This also likely explains why ROE (17.5%) looks meaningfully better than ROCE (10.4%): the gap is consistent with a combination of financial leverage (debt of Rs 27,892 crore) and the other-income boost flowing through net income more than through core operating returns. Contingent liabilities of Rs 13,859 crore are sizeable, as is common for large PSU miners with tax, land-acquisition and environmental-clearance disputes, and are worth noting as a standing risk rather than an active crisis absent further specifics. The government's stake has declined 2.73 points recently (now 69.47%), consistent with a routine disinvestment-linked stake sale rather than a promoter-distress signal.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold on both windows and fresh research supports that: a mature, slow-growing PSU core business with a genuine but incremental renewable-diversification catalyst, where reported profit growth is meaningfully flattered by a large other-income line that should not be extrapolated as core operating strength. This combination of low core growth, quality-adjusted earnings, and a real but modest new-growth lever is a straightforward Hold, with no basis found for anything more or less cautious.
summary: NLC India is a government-owned lignite mining and power generation company that is now expanding into renewable energy, including a newly awarded 900 MW solar project. The core mining and power business grows slowly, and a meaningful part of this year's reported profit came from non-core other income (such as interest earnings) rather than from the core mining/power operations, so the headline profit growth overstates the underlying business's momentum somewhat. We rate it a Hold: a stable, mature PSU utility with a real but incremental renewable growth story layered on top, at earnings that include a notable non-core boost.
positive_para: A newly awarded 900 MW solar project (GUVNL LoI, July 2026) is a genuine, verifiable step in diversifying beyond the legacy lignite/thermal base into renewables, aligned with national energy-transition policy and adding a real incremental growth lever. As a Navratna PSU, the company benefits from stable, largely regulated revenue streams and government backing that reduce business-continuity risk relative to a purely merchant power/mining operator.
negative_para: A substantial Rs 1,887 crore of other income in FY26 has been flagged as inflating reported earnings, meaning core mining/power operating performance is weaker than the headline profit and ROE figures suggest -- this is a genuine earnings-quality point, not a technicality, and should temper how much of the reported 38% TTM profit growth is credited to the underlying business. Core growth itself has been slow for years (5-year sales growth just 12%, 3-year quant revenue CAGR near 2.7%), and sizeable contingent liabilities (Rs 13,859 crore) are a standing, if not immediately active, risk typical of a large PSU miner.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a modest valuation (value_score 89.4 in the quant data, reflecting a low multiple) the market is not pricing much growth into this name, which is appropriate given the slow core-business growth rate once the other-income boost is stripped out of the earnings picture; the 900 MW solar addition is a genuine positive but too small relative to the company's existing scale to change the growth character on its own. Fair value for a mature, income-oriented PSU utility, not a re-rating candidate on current information.

technical_commentary: A two-stage story: an initial base-and-breakout (2021-23, Rs52 to Rs253) was followed by roughly two years of genuinely choppy sideways consolidation (Rs207-290) before a fresh breakout this year to an all-time high of Rs388 (May-2026, on volume more than double the prior year's average -- a well-confirmed push). Currently correcting 22.5% off that high with the MA stack still bullish (10>20>40). The long consolidation phase keeps this from scoring as a clean trender, but the volume-confirmed breakout is a real positive.
